title: Demand Response Programs Event Notice Periods and Channels — Quick Reference
content:
**Notice before an event.** Each of the Demand Response Programs gives notice of an event the stated number of hours before the event starts, through the channels shown.

| Program | Notice before the event starts | How the notice is delivered |
|---|---|---|
| Peak Time Rebate | 24 hours | Email, text and automated call |
| Smart Thermostat Rewards | 2 hours | Thermostat display and app notification |
| AC Cycling Program | 0 hours | None required; events are posted on the company website |
| Home Battery Dispatch | 24 hours | Battery app notification and email |
| Commercial Capacity Bidding Program | 24 hours | Email and automated call to the designated contacts |
| Base Interruptible Program | 0.5 hours (30 minutes) | Automated call and text to the designated contacts |

**Points to note**

- The AC Cycling Program gives no advance notice (0 hours); its events are posted on the company website, and no individual notice is required.
- The Base Interruptible Program gives the shortest notice of the programs that notify customers — 0.5 hours — by automated call and text to the customer's designated contacts.
- The two business programs notify the customer's designated contacts: the Commercial Capacity Bidding Program by email and automated call with 24 hours' notice, the Base Interruptible Program by automated call and text with 0.5 hours' notice.

**Illustration (hypothetical start times).** For a Peak Time Rebate event starting at 15:00 on a Thursday, notice is given 24 hours before the start, at 15:00 on the Wednesday. For a Smart Thermostat Rewards event starting at 16:00, notice is given on the thermostat display and in the app 2 hours before the start, at 14:00 the same day. For a Base Interruptible Program event starting at 10:00, the designated contacts are called and texted 0.5 hours before the start, at 09:30.
